x-bump-note: 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0 widens `applies_to` from `state/roadmap/*/OVERVIEW.md` to `state/roadmap/**/OVERVIEW.md`. No property is added, removed, or made required and no existing value's semantics change — the widen only admits nested roadmap directories (a sprint-scoped roadmap living under a subdirectory of `state/roadmap/`) into the match set, and every path that matched under 1.3.0 still matches. Verified against the live matcher rather than assumed (claude-klabauter `coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py` `_glob_to_regex`/`match_schema`): the widened glob is a strict superset that additionally admits a top-level `state/roadmap/OVERVIEW.md`, and no other registered schema's glob competes for any path it matches — checked by loading the whole registry, not by eyeballing prefixes. Note the widen also moves this entry LATER in the `_byGlob` specificity order (that sort keys on wildcard count ascending), which is why the no-competing-glob check is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Precedent for classing an applies_to widen MINOR rather than major: peer-set-entry.schema.json 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, same shape of change. LOCKSTEP — a consumer that decides which files ARE roadmap records by its own glob must widen in the same edit, or a nested roadmap validates while staying invisible to that consumer: `artifact-shape-contract.schema.json`'s `x-coordinator-applies_to` mirror, `docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md`'s registry table row, and `tests/test_artifact_corpus_validates_against_schema.py`'s `_CORPUS_SCHEMA_MAP` all carry the same glob and moved together here. MOTIVATING ASK: claude-klabauter's roadmap/sprint-split work (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-21-claude-klabauter-em-roadmap-schema-glob-widen-and-spine-schema-homing.md). Vendoring order: DoE lands first and they re-vendor on our ping, because the bump originates here. 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 added the optional nullable top-level `deliverable_id` scalar (durable deliverable-spine join key; C9a). DR-097 push-side notification duty is discharged — memo delivered to claude-klabauter-em 2026-08-10 at their `8796e9bd4`. Vendoring order actually used: DoE lands first, claude-klabauter vendors on our ping, because this bump originates here. 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 dropped the `null` arm from `suggested_priority` (was `anyOf: [enum, null]`, now a plain closed enum) — review finding: the field's own description already argues absence covers 'no suggestion', so `null` was a second, redundant representation of that state. Classified MAJOR because a document that previously set `suggested_priority: null` explicitly now fails validation; no on-disk corpus was found using that value as of this bump (grepped state/ and docs/ 2026-07-27), so the practical blast radius is believed zero, but the schema's stated domain narrowed. 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 added the optional top-level `suggested_priority` scalar (advisory EM priority signal, C2).
description: Roadmap — forward horizon/portfolio overview record. Validates OVERVIEW.md files only; spinoff-roadmap stub cross-field rules ride on the handoff schema.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Example-repo portfolio vocabulary: planning/active/blocked/shipped/archived. Roadmap-planning OVERVIEW vocabulary: draft/shape-approved/final-approved.

owner.description: Owner identifier (person or team) responsible for this roadmap.

items.description: Plan slugs or stub_ids this roadmap tracks.

blocked_by.description: roadmap_id values this roadmap is gated by.

roadmap_id.description: Unique identifier for this roadmap node.

stub_id.description: Stub code identifier (e.g. Example-initiative-3) used in cross-references.

shape_approved_by.description: Identifier of who approved the shape.

final_approved_by.description: Identifier of who gave final approval.

initiative.description: FK to state/initiatives/<id>.yaml. Nullable — absent or null means this roadmap is not yet attached to a named initiative. A non-null value must be a non-empty initiative id (e.g. 'example-fleet-pro-launch'). Spec backlink: pln-initiative-govern-sweep-priori-6cf808 § C0

suggested_priority.description: Advisory execution-priority signal an EM may attach to this roadmap at authoring time. Optional (not nullable — absence already covers 'no suggestion'; a redundant null representation was reviewed out, see Finding 4 / review-integrator). Enum is the priority-ledger domain (priority-ledger.schema.json's urgent|high|medium|low|none) MINUS 'none' — an EM has no reason to author an explicit clear; absence of the field already covers that case. Advisory only: the PM-owned priority ledger (state/priority-ledger/) is the authoritative tier and lives on a deliberately separate surface — this field never overrides it, and that separation (not memory) is what keeps 'advisory never overrides authoritative' structural. Do NOT add a pm_priority field to this frontmatter to compensate; the tier split is the point. NEGATIVE-SPEC: no inherited_from / priority_predecessor field is permitted on this frontmatter either — priority does not chain roadmap-to-roadmap. No backfill of pre-existing roadmaps, consistent with the handoff schema's origin_* no-backfill policy.

deliverable_id.description: The durable deliverable join key, minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact; null or absent when this record predates the spine. Spec backlink: pln-sizing-objects-join-the-delive-0fcd0a § C9a
